fixAssessment.addressedExplanation: The blocking bug from round 1 is confirmed fixed in /root/benchmark-scripts/coding_agent_bench.py. Line 392-396 now correctly computes aggregate_decode_tok_per_s = total_decode_tokens / wall_clock_seconds where wall_clock_seconds = end_time - start_time (wall clock time). The corrected Qwen3.5-9B baseline-report.json shows aggregate values scaling correctly with concurrency: c1=21.39 tok/s, c2=41.71 tok/s (~2x), c4=82.73 tok/s (~4x). This is the correct behavior.
remainingConcerns: Llama-2-7b-hf coding agent benchmarks were NOT re-run with the fixed script. The baseline-report.json shows Llama-2-7b-hf coding_agent data with wall_clock_seconds=0 and aggregate=avg (c1=36.1, c2=36.01, c4=36.06 - same value across all concurrency levels), indicating the old pre-fix data is still used. No _fixed.json files exist for Llama-2-7b-hf in /root/benchmark-results/.
The library document at .factory/library/environment.md still contains the stale 'Known metric issue' note describing the bug as if it were unfixed, even though the fix is now in place.

The output_throughput_tok_per_s, request_throughput, and total_token_throughput values appear correct, so this is a metric extraction issue for request counts only.

summary: Feature PASS. The primary blocking issue (aggregate_decode_tok_per_s bug in coding_agent_bench.py) is confirmed fixed and Qwen3.5-9B baseline data is correct. Two non-blocking issues remain: (1) Llama-2-7b-hf coding agent benchmarks were not re-run so baseline-report.json still has incorrect aggregate values for that model, and (2) the library document has a stale bug note. The main mission goal — establishing a valid Qwen3.5-9B baseline for optimization comparisons — is satisfied.
